title: Browns expect to name starting QB on Monday; Deshaun Watson’s comments won’t impact decision
content:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken anticipates naming a starting quarterback Monday and said Deshaun Watson’s postgame comments will not impact his decision.

“I think he emptied his heart a little bit and I don’t think that says who he is,” Monken said Sunday. “I think the moment just got him after the game and it can get all of us.”

Watson has been competing with Shedeur Sanders for the starting job. He has been erratic throughout July and August before bottoming out in Saturday’s preseason game against the Bills’ backups when he was 5 of 12 for 35 yards and an interception. Watson was booed loudly on multiple occasions in his first game back in Cleveland since twice tearing his Achilles despite it being a sparse crowd. Watson said after the game the boos felt personal.

“I think the whole world knows, it has nothing to do with the performance. It’s a little more personal than that,” Watson said. “I think that’s a disrespectful thing.”

Watson noted how he was cheered by some Browns fans when he left the field on a cart after he tore his Achilles two years ago.

“It’s a mental battle every day,” Watson said. “I feel like I get more love on road games than I do at home games. … I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in, being around the facility, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person I know I am and the character would help, and I guess it hasn’t. So that’s why I say it’s more personal.”

Watson was acquired by the Browns in 2022 and signed to the largest guaranteed contract in NFL history after he was accused by more than two dozen women of sexual assault or other forms of sexual misconduct, mostly involving massage appointments. He has denied wrongdoing and two Texas grand juries declined to indict him. He settled more than 20 civil lawsuits filed against him and the NFL suspended him for 11 games in 2022.

Injuries have limited Watson to 19 games over his first four seasons in Cleveland, but he still could be named the starter Monday for what is his final season under contract with the Browns.

“All I’ve seen from him is a player that’s worked awfully hard to get back to where he is now and given himself a chance to compete at the highest level,” Monken said. “I’ve been really pleased with how he’s worked, how he’s approached every day.”

The Browns open the season with two road games. Monken said if they play well and win, the boos will dissipate.

“What I’m concerned about is us playing well as a team and on offense,” Monken said. “When you play well, none of the other stuff matters.”
